title: refactor-presubmit-runtime-and-lockfile-minimizer
author: Leah Park
release_notes: Lightweight presubmit runtime (Go) and lockfile minimizer reduce CI wall time and devdep churn; no runtime behavior changes to production artifacts.
description: Context: Our presubmit pipeline has been slow to start and brittle when large devdependency trees are present. This PR refactors the presubmit runner into a single small Go binary and adds a lockfile-minimizer tool that produces a trimmed dev-lockfile used only for CI. Motivation: improve feedback time for incremental dev changes, reduce transient flakes from devdep installs, and make presubmit more amenable to container caching. Changes summary: - New presubmit runner: ci/presubmit/main.go and cmd/presubmit/ (replaces a 600-line Bash script). The runner performs fast path detection, sparse test selection, and a short-lived local cache warm step. - Lockfile minimizer: tools/lockfile-minimizer/* (Go). Scans package-lock/pnpm/yarn lock, keeps only entries referenced by devprofiles (lint, test, bench) and outputs ci/dev-lock.json. - CI wiring: .github/workflows/presubmit.yml updated to use the minimizer artifact and the Go runner image; Dockerfile.ci introduced to keep images small. - Docs and runbook: docs/ci/presubmit-runbook.md with operational notes and rollback steps. Checklist: [x] Replace Bash presubmit with Go runner (ci/presubmit) [x] Add lockfile-minimizer and integration into presubmit job [x] Add container image and publish step to internal registry [x] Update runbook and emergency toggle [x] Add telemetry tags to trace slow presubmit runs What changed (high level): commits: - build: introduce presubmit Go runner and tests - feat: add lockfile minimizer and unit tests - ci: publish ci image and use minimizer artifact in workflow - refactor: remove old bash presubmit script and adapters - docs: presubmit runbook and rollback playbook Files of interest (small sample): - ci/presubmit/main.go — new runner that dispatches lint/test/bench fast paths - tools/lockfile-minimizer/minimizer.go — lockfile trimming logic (supports package-lock.json and pnpm-lock.yaml) - .github/workflows/presubmit.yml — swapped to use ci container and minimizer artifact - docker/ci/Dockerfile.ci — small Go runtime image - scripts/ci/publish-image.sh — publish image and tag by sha How it was validated: - Local unit tests: minimizer unit tests (92% coverage on parsing heuristics) - Integration smoke: ran presubmit job against a synthetic repo subset; median startup time reduced from ~38s to ~9s (cold) in Docker CI images; full run throughput improved by ~18% in our nightly bench. - Canary: enabled for 25% of branches via workflow flag for 3 days; no failures tied to minimizer output observed. Backwards compatibility: The minimizer only produces a CI-only lockfile; production build pipelines continue to use the canonical lockfile. The Go runner preserves same exit codes and expected environment variables. Rollout: - Step 1: publish ci image and minimizer artifact (this PR) - Step 2: enable 25% branch canary for 72h (done) - Step 3: ramp to 100% and remove legacy script (done via this merge) Follow-ups / TODOs: - Add deterministic minimizer seed to force reproducible outputs (ENG-3301) - Add retry/backoff to artifact fetch in presubmit runner (INF-219) - Consider stable prebuilt image caching in regionally distributed registries (INF-307)
commit_summary: build(ci): add presubmit Go runner and unit tests
feat(ci): add lockfile-minimizer to trim devdeps
ci: publish ci image to internal registry and use it in workflow
refactor(ci): remove legacy bash presubmit script
docs(ci): presubmit runbook and rollback playbook

notes: This PR intentionally keeps the CI-only lockfile out of production pipelines. The minimizer will be iterated upon—ENG-3301 tracks determinism and reproducibility. Image size reduction is ~42% relative to previous presubmit container.
operational_impacts: Ops: add image retention rules for ci images older than 90 days; Security: scan minimizer binary in supply-chain checks (already in CI).
